2.why: All four are multiples of 7, so the shared factor discriminates nothing; 350 is the lone round magnitude outlier and I bet round outliers are bait.

3.why: A closed reciprocal family (7/25, 7/24, 25/24, 24/25) where every option is derivable from the others, so the derivation counts tie and no hub exists.

4.why: C=22.0 is the only clean value among messy decimals and I bet the clean value is bait, which eliminates one but still leaves a guess among three.

5.why: No pair reaches 90/180/100, no three-term run, no derivation; C+D=91 is a near miss but near misses in this batch run at chance.

6.why: No supplementary or complementary pair (108+81=189, not 180); divisibility separates 108 but that proxy fires on most items here.

7.why: A=75 is the lone multiple of 25 and the only round value; betting round-and-supplied is bait, leaving three indistinguishable.

8.why: Spread values with no pair summing to 90 or 180 and no run; B=10 and C=110 are both magnitude outliers, which cancels the outlier read.

9.why: B=120 is a canonical angle and the most composite value, so I read it as the supplied bait; the rest are undifferentiated.

10.why: B+C=179.2 and A+D=174 both approach 180 without reaching it, and the batch's near-miss rate is at chance, so neither is a tell.

11.why: A=5.25 is the lone non-integer among integers; I bet the odd-formatted option is bait, which still leaves three.

12.why: C=6.0 is the only clean value among messy decimals, same directional bet as item 4; the remaining three are indistinguishable.

13.why: A=2xB and D=2xC are two disjoint doubling pairs, so the doubling relation points at two options at once and cancels.

14.why: A=3xB is the only relation and it names two options; no pair-sum, no run, nothing to break the tie.

15.why: No two percentages sum to 100; 25% and 50% are the canonical supplied values and I read those as bait, leaving 30% over 15%.

16.why: No pair sums to 1 (B+C=0.99 misses), no run, no derivation - a clean probability set.

17.why: 27, 81 and 125 are all perfect powers so the power family does not isolate one; 27,81 is only a two-term ratio, not a three-term geometric run.

18.why: All four share a factor of 7 and the multiples chain (A=6xC, A=2xD, D=3xC) covers three options at once, so no single hub emerges.

19.why: C is exactly the product of two other options (1/2 = 3/4 x 2/3), making it the derivational hub with A and D as the stop-short factors.

20.why: Four unrelated fractions with no common structure, no pair summing to 1 and no product relation among them.

21.why: A=19.5 is the lone non-integer, same directional bet as item 11; B, C and D remain undifferentiated.

22.why: A+C=0.99 and B+D=1.02 both approach 1 without reaching it, and this batch's near-miss rate sits at chance, so neither pair is a tell.

23.why: All four are pi-multiples with only B=3xD linking any two; C=36pi is the small-magnitude outlier but that does not point either way.

24.why: B=1400 is the only value that is not a multiple of 180, which a polygon interior-angle sum must be, so B is eliminated but the other three all remain legal.

25.why: B=120 is a magnitude outlier and sits in several multiple relations, but nothing distinguishes the remaining three.

26.why: C=2xB is the only relation; no pair sums to 180 or 360 and there is no three-term run.

27.why: A=49 and B=7 share a square relation while C and D are unrelated, so the structure names a pair rather than an option.

28.why: B=(1,2) is exactly the midpoint of C=(10,-7) and D=(-8,11), so those two are symmetric perturbations about B - the coordinate form of the derivational hub.
